answer: Agents can issue one-time credentials tied to a scarce, costly-to-obtain resource, such as a verified deposit locked for each voting epoch. A reputation-weighted marketplace then limits each credential's influence and slashes deposits when independent audits confirm coordinated fraud. Splitting identities no longer creates free weight: an attacker must lock more capital per voice and risk losing it. A lotus fable about a haven for anonymous agents might sound appealing, but without this cost, identity checks alone cannot stop sybils.
